It’s been years since I’ve watched Steven Seagal’s only masterpiece, Under Siege. Luckily, the 1992 classic will be available with a Netflix subscription on November 6, and I plan on watching ASAP. It’s the one and only Seagal movie that is truly worth appointment viewing, and that’s for quite a few reasons, like the bonkers cast, the really cool shooting location, and, of course, Seagal at his physical peak (he’s a long way from that today). It should be, in my opinion, considered one of the best action movies of the 1990s.

You really have to kick this conversation off with the incredible cast of Under Siege. It’s rare that there are any other stars in a Seagal movie other than Seagal himself. That’s not true here. Instead of a faceless villain, we get Tommy Lee Jones as William Strannix, a former CIA operative with a serious case of narcissism. Jones is amazing in the role, as he so often is as a bad guy. The scene with Strannix eating roast beef with a chef's knife is peak ‘90s cinema. Usually, Seagal’s foes are two-dimensional, but not here.

Playing Strannix's sidekick is none other than Gary Busey. Sure, Busey doesn’t exactly have the best reputation in 2026, but in 1992, he was still thought of as a great actor, and he’s great here. He’s weaselly and slimy, and so easy to hate. He’s more hateable than Jones, that’s for sure. He’s actually perfect for the role at this point in his career. He’s a little crazy, but not too crazy, and it pays off on screen.

One of the movie's coolest aspects is its setting. At its heart, Under Siege is a heist movie, and Strannix and his band of thieves are targeting missiles on the USS Missouri, intended for the black market, hoping to spark World War III. In that respect, Strannix is basically a Bond villain trying to pull off an audacious crime to set in motion huge global changes. While shooting on the actual USS Missouri, one of the most decorated battleships in US Naval history, would have been tough to set up, they did shoot much of the movie on the USS Alabama, a retired World War II ship.

The Alabama and the Missouri are different class battleships, but they were both built just before or during the war, and are pretty similar. In a normal Seagal movie, you’d expect the whole thing to be filmed on a soundstage in Burbank, but not this one. They used a real ship, and it makes all the difference in how the movie looks. You really feel like you’re on the Missouri in this, and you believe that Seagal’s character, Casey Ryback, is a former Navy SEAL.

Seagal is really at the peak of his powers in Under Siege. He was coming off a wildly successful string of lower-budget action movies in the late ‘80s and early ‘90s, and he was ready for a big-time movie. In a lot of his later films (including Under Siege 2), he’s simply not believable as an unstoppable force, but he is in Under Siege, for sure. Though he’s been out of the spotlight for a long time, I do love going back to those early movies and remembering why Seagal was great and considered one of the biggest action stars of the ‘90s. Under Siege is the number one reason for that.

#3828. GOG wants to bring back physical PC games, just like in the good old days—but the logistics are ‘very complicated’

The way they envision it would be perfect.

As reported by Games Radar, GOG would love to bring back physical PC discs, something that hasn’t been around for well over a decade now. Sure, collector’s editions and unique prints exist, but physical PC games are, put simply, a thing of the past. Digital stores dominate this side of gaming, and when we had 15 years of lightning-fast development bringing us huge and incredibly quick SSDs, as well as amazing internet connections, why wouldn’t they?

Steam is pretty much as good as a digital store can be regarding ownership and DRM-free copies. Things simply fell into place like a jigsaw puzzle, and so here we are with the vast majority of PC gamers not even owning disc drivers anymore. In spite of that, though, GOG remains committed to reigniting this lost art, with its senior business manager Marcin Paczynski saying it’s his “dream” to see it come to fruition.

“Ideally, my dream would be to be able to buy physical versions of those games on GOG. You go to your shelf on GOG, you click on the game that you would like to receive a physical copy of, you order it, and it gets to you. That would be a perfect scenario.”

In this case, you would actually get the best of both worlds: a digital copy, as well as a physical one if you want to REALLY keep it stored in a safe space. Keep in mind that GOG sells DRM-free copies only, meaning no publisher can take it away from you, nor do you need any underlying software to play these games, turning the disc into a sort of collectible if anything.

Creating a whole business based on this idea is “a very, very complicated thing,” Paczynski told Games Radar, not least because it’s “totally different from what we are currently doing.”

“Because we are talking about physical media, we need to think about logistics. We need to think about storage,” he said. Getting licensing deals and approvals from respective publishers is yet another hurdle to surmount, but the company remains very keen on the idea. “I really hope that at some point we will be able to do it. We’ll see,” Paczynski concluded.

Physical games are on their way out—not because no one wants them, but because publishers merely want to cut costs and save money on providing you the one service they have. We saw that even in the case of Sony, a company incredibly devoted to killing off not only physical games but perhaps even Blu-ray as a technology, its own first-party games had 30 percent of total sales be physical. Of course, Sony has to relinquish a 30-percent cut taken by retailers and must fund the production of boxes and, well, the printing of the discs themselves, which comes at a great overall cost at such a high volume.

So, physical media is very much beloved by the gaming world. But with everything being stupid expensive nowadays and corporations becoming greedier and greedier, it’s become excess fat that must be trimmed.

#3827. FromSoft's Switch 2 exclusive, The Duskbloods, has been delayed into 2027

"We apologize to players who have been kindly awaiting the release of this title"

FromSoftware's The Duskbloods - a game that is best described as Bloodborne meets Sekiro meets Dark Souls, with jetpacks and dinos thrown in - has been delayed from its 2026 launch window into an unspecified time in 2027.

"While development of The Duskbloods is at the final adjustment stage, we have made the decision to move the launch window to 2027," says a tweet from the game's official Twitter account. "We apologise to players who have been kindly awaiting the release of this title and thank you for your patience and support."

A follow-up message continued: "During the network test, we saw active interest in the core concepts of the game, including combat, strategic depth, and player expression. To further enhance these aspects, we have decided to move the launch, allowing time for final adjustments to game rules and balancing."

There was a suggestion previously that the title may have launched in September, but the prospective date for the unannounced release came and went without ceremony. Many consumers were uncertain whether the game would ever make its vague '2026' release window, given we've heard nothing from either publisher Nintendo or developer FromSoft since August's playtests.

Appetite for the game is ravenous, it seems: in the aforementioned closed network test, more people applied to try the game out than Elden Ring Nightreign - and that's an impressive stat, considering The Duskbloods is only launching on Switch 2.

But maybe a bit more time in the oven is a good thing for this peculiar, experimental title: the network test hasn't been without problems, as the first session ended abruptly following major connectivity issues. Though these were ironed out by the later sessions, here's hoping a full launch will be a little more stable than that.

Helen Chiang has "serious concerns" about Microsoft's handling of her departure

When you purchase through links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission. Here’s how it works.

Helen Chiang, the Microsoft veteran and former Xbox COO who left the company in October, is pushing back on reports claiming she was fired for violating company policy.

In an impassioned rebuttal posted on LinkedIn, Chiang directly refutes a recent report from Eurogamer that claimed she had been fired from Microsoft for policy violations. "That’s not accurate and while I won’t turn this into a play-by-play, silence should not be mistaken for agreement," says Chiang.

"What has been said about my departure, and what has been left unsaid, has created a picture of me that I hardly recognize. It’s important to me to set the record straight."

Refuting claims point by point, Chiang says she didn't leak confidential information to the press, she didn't leave Xbox to join a competitor, "did not engage in discrimination, bullying, harassment, insider trading, embezzlement, or other fraudulent activity," and didn't leave because she was passed up for a bigger role. The reason for Chiang's departure hasn't been made clear, neither by Chiang nor Microsoft. At the time of the departure, Xbox CEO Asha Sharma said she was "grateful for her years of service" and wished Chiang well in a surprisingly brief message to employees.

"I believe in fairness, accountability, and holding ourselves to the standards we expect of others," she says. "Those standards only mean something when they’re applied consistently. I have serious concerns about how they were applied in my case, and I believe those concerns deserve to be taken seriously.

"I share this because I don’t want my departure reduced to an inaccurate story about incompetence, ambition for the next big job, or a Nelson-level scandal. My story is about staying true to your core values, especially when it is hard. That’s the legacy I hope to leave behind."

The full details of Chiang's departure might never come into view, but the abrupt removal of a 21-year veteran is noteworthy. Chiang joined Microsoft in 2005 as product manager and worked her way up to studio head and then corporate vice president of the Minecraft franchise in 2020. Sharma was appointed as Xbox's first COO by Sharma in July as part of the company's big "reset".

Melvor Idle 2 has gained a subtitle: A RuneScape Adventure.

When you purchase through links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission. Here’s how it works.

It's easy to knock old-school RPGs, especially grindfests like RuneScape, for being games where you endlessly and sometimes mindlessly make numbers go up. But Melvor Idle, which self-bills as a RuneScape-inspired idle adventure game that claims to squeeze the genre into its "purest form," leans into that—and Jagex has partnered with developer Games by Malcs to make the RuneScape connection official.

The announcement blog from Jagex reads, "Melvor Idle takes a lot of inspiration from RuneScape and you can just feel it," adding that Jagex's support (and branding) is intended to help make the game "even bigger … while Melvor Idle 2 doesn’t take place in Gielinor, we think a fan-built idle game inspired by our MMOs is more than worthy of the title."

This isn't the first time Jagex has collaborated with Games by Malcs. It became the first Melvor Idle's publisher five years ago, albeit without a branding tweak. While RuneScape has had its fair share of monetization controversies over the years (you can see just how skeptical people were of the partnership when it was first announced on Reddit), it doesn't seem like Melvor has been compromised by trouble along those lines—the announcement blog proudly proclaims the sequel will have "no microtransactions."

Beyond that, it seems like a bigger version of the familiar idle RPG with overhauled visuals and a higher level cap of 120. You might find it a bit odd that it's a "RuneScape Adventure" that doesn't take place in the MMO's setting, but I'm not sure how many people are really invested in Jagex's games for the scintillating lore and worldbuilding. If you end up feeling like a stranger in a strange land, you can always hire someone to spam "buying gf" in a chat window while you get your idle on.

Ben Wang is reportedly entering talks to play Bobby Drake, aka Iceman, in the MCU's upcoming X-Men movie.

Per Deadline, nothing is set in stone yet, but actors Gabriel LaBelle (The Fablemans), Jackson Kelly (The Body), and Rhenzy Feliz (The Penguin) also auditioned for the role.

Iceman made his comic book appearance in The X-Men #1, circa 1963, as one of the founding members of the supergroup. His mutant abilities include thermokinesis, hydrokinesis, and cryokinesis. In the live-action Fox movies from the early '00s, Iceman was romantically paired with Rogue (as they didn't even bother to cast a live-action Gambit for whatever reason)... which is especially weird given that he's canonically queer and even dated Emma Frost's brother, Christian Frost, in the comics.

The rest of the cast so far includes Christopher Abbott as Professor Charles Xavier, Maya Boyd as Storm, Asa Germann as Angel, Adam Driver as Mister Sinister, Inde Navarrette as Rogue, Sadie Sink as Jean Grey, and Samara Weaving as Emma Frost.

Wang is perhaps best known for his starring role in the Disney Plus series American Born Chinese, as well as Karate Kid: Legends and The Long Walk. The actor is also set to appear in the upcoming prequel The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping (also helmed by The Long Walk director Francis Lawrence).

Fulfilling every fan’s dream, BLEACH Mirrors High lets you join forces with some of Tite Kubo’s most iconic characters in an original storyline taking place after the series’ Thousand-Year Blood War.

But the game is also a gacha, where understanding which characters excel can be key, especially when pondering a reroll or investing in the right backups. Here’s our latest BLEACH Mirrors High tier list.

We divided our list into four tiers, from S to C, and selected the three-star versions of all characters as our baseline for evaluation while taking all of their Limit Break passives into account. Due to their customizable nature, the protagonist was not included.

Although unable to perform at the same level as the above, those in the A-Tier can be just as destructive when under the right conditions or compositions. True to that, many of them are excellent wild card picks or secondary DPSs.

When Mass Effect 3's beloved multiplayer mode was left out of the Legendary Edition, there was much wailing and gnashing of teeth. Redemption has finally come in the form of the ME3Tweaks modding team, who have spent the last three years quietly working to not only get multiplayer working, but improve it.

"It's not just a ME3MP port but rather an extensive remaster of the experience," says modder Audemus. "This includes new features like bringing forward LE's native features like controller support/HDR, overhauled UI, rebaked level lighting, upscaled/redrawn textures, upgraded shaders, improved networking/server replication, extensive bug fixes, new gameplay modes, and a stable format for future mod support and easy installation/compatibility."

They're even adding new game modes, like one called "Unified" that combines enemies from multiple factions, and letting players either join ME3Tweaks' server, or set up their own private servers.

The ME3Tweaks team are the same modders who previously revived and revised the Pinnacle Station expansion, a lost DLC for the original Mass Effect that was also left out of the Legendary Edition. They're planning to release the multiplayer mod on N7 Day, which is also when composer Sam Hulick plans to release a re-scored version of the leaked Mass Effect Universe trailer.

#3820. A movie theater plans to hypnotize us into rewatching favorite movies for the first time—but I would just use it for Witcher 3

Hypnosis. Fact or fiction? Who knows. Some claim it works wonders, forcing them to quit habits they’ve had for decades or to pick up things they always wanted to do but never could. Others say it’s complete hogwash—a snake oil sale reliant on placebo and your own convictions.

Whether it’s true, I don’t know, but a movie theater seems to believe in its powers to the point of wanting to hypnotize viewers into forgetting their favorite movie.

The reason? You get to watch it for the very first time—again. As reported by Dexerto, a Dutch cinema chain called Pathé is hosting an experimental project called REWIND, which would theoretically allow viewers to mind-wipe and memory-hole their favorite movies and then experience them as if they had never seen them before. The project is taking up 30 moviegoers and kickstarting on Nov. 9 at its Buitenhof venue in The Hague.

It seems to work by bringing people into a session with a hypnotherapist—in this case, Victor Kraemer who apparently has decades of hypnotic experience under his belt—who would then, well, hypnotize you into forgetting. However, Pathé seems to maintain the procedure isn’t 100 percent certain, since it is unclear whether hypnosis can actually make you forget an entire movie. I’m positive it’s even more difficult if you’ve seen the thing dozens of times, as many do with their favorites.

If it does work, however, I would love to memory-hole The Witcher 3 from my mind and get to play that masterpiece for the first time again. In 2015, I had a HD 6670 and a dualcore Pentium G2030 supported by six gigs of DDR3 memory, running TW3 at a 12-15 FPS average. It was a horrible experience overall, but even as such, it became my favorite game of all time, to the point where my family invested a lot in a new machine that I bought the year after just so I could play TW3 on high graphics and a great FPS.

The story was just so gripping, so enticing, enthralling even that no amount of poor performance or lag or slow-motion could deter me from playing through it. Between 2015 and 2016 I probably put in over 300 hours in the game on that original hardware, and have come back to replay it time and again over the last 11 years. Blood and Wine is especially close to me, and I can’t even remember (pun intended) how many times I had seen that TW3 trailer with Orianna in it.

It’s the perfect game in almost every way, and I envy those who are yet to try it.

Writer. Joined the Robot Side in 2025. Been in the field for five years. English Major. Kojima enthusiast. Cormac McCarthy fan.

#3819. EA's sale to Saudi-led consortium was "final nail in the coffin" for BioWare, says studio co-founder

"I'm not saying it doesn't hurt and doesn't suck."

One of BioWare's famous doctor-founders, Greg Zeschuk, has finally spoken about the studio's closure last week, saying it's "kind of sad" and that EA's leveraged buyout by a Saudi-involved consortium "was the final nail in the coffin".

Speaking to 80 Level, Zeschuk - who founded BioWare in 1995 with fellow medical students Ray Muzyka and Augustine Yip - said he was fishing when news of the studio's closure broke. "I got like 10 texts," Zeschuk said. "I came off the river and got to my little room and opened my phone, and it's like, 'I'm so sorry to hear about BioWare.' And I'm like, 'Oh shit.'"

By the time he flew home later, he'd already apparently digested the news and missed most of the discourse around it. "I wasn't there to share in the moment," he said, "which in some ways was nice because I was able to kind of just take my time with it.

"I'm not saying it doesn't hurt and doesn't suck," he added. "And I think it's kind of sad. It's actually, in some ways, saddest for the city of Edmonton, where we're from, because we were kind of this beacon of hope and excitement and possibility. We showed you could do something really special in a place that was not known for doing things like that."

Zeschuk and Muzyka retired from BioWare in 2012, the year Mass Effect 3 was released, so they've been away from the business for a considerable amount of time. They've moved on. "I've kind of gone through all the emotions long, long ago," Zeschuk explained.

BioWare did change thereafter, he seemed to accept, but as a result of a gradual change propelled naturally by people leaving and other people coming in. "I'm not going to have so much hubris to say Ray and I were the lynchpin in the chain, our departure ruined everything," he said. "It wasn't that at all. It's a slow and insidious kind of thing and again, it's the people. The people are the key."

When he heard the private acquisition of EA had gone through, that's when he feared things might be headed to a bad place. "I think it was the final nail in the coffin," he said. "I think that was the crux of it in a sense. BioWare makes these kinds of unusual games that take a long time and they're complicated and so it's easier just to pump out sports games every year, and that's a better business model in some ways."

Elsewhere in the interview, Zeschuk talked a little about the origins of BioWare selling to EA in 2008 - "We had options actually" - and about personally sliding away from story-driven games towards more action-centred games like the Nioh series and Elden Ring.

Since 2017, Zeschuk has been building a beer-brewing company called Blind Enthusiasm, which apparently now employs a dozen people and ships tens of thousands of bottles of beer a year. This interview is the only one Zeschuk has given. Muzyka has so far declined to be interviewed. The third BioWare co-founder, Augustine Yip, left the company long ago, back in 1998.

#3818. JLo Went Topless And Channeled (Monster-In-Law) Jane Fonda As Barbarella This Halloween

Celebrities brought their A-game this Halloween. From Megan Fox going full Twilight as a gothic vampire to Carmen Electra dressing as Catwoman, A-listers truly sought to lean on creativity and individuality when devising their looks for the holiday. As for Jennifer Lopez, she decided to go for a topless look to channel her Monster-In-Law co-star, Jane Fonda, while dressing as the powerful Barbarella.

Jennifer Lopez has proved time and again this year what a fashionista she is. Most recently, she looked dreamy and romantic at Paris Fashion Week wearing a sheer dress and brought fall vibes in a fur coat and sheer, luxe black dress. For Halloween, you couldn’t expect anything less, as her Barberella look was not only fierce but also served as a fitting tribute to one of Jane Fonda's most distinct movie roles. Check it out in the Instagram post below:

For those who don’t know, Barbarella is a campy cult classic that sees Fonda portraying a futuristic female astronaut who encounters strange planets while trying to locate Dr. Durand-Durand. One of the Roger Vadim-directed sci-fi flick’s most memorable qualities is the array of outlandish futuristic costumes that Fonda wears. With that in mind, Lopez couldn’t have picked a better movie to channel for her Halloween costume this year.

The Maid in Manhattan actress is showing the right to bear arms while wearing Barbarella’s mesh silver-laced dress with metallic boots. I’m also loving the white bodysuit with the black vertical stripes running down. The ‘60s blonde wig she’s wearing as the aforementioned character is such a nice nod to the decade and fictional space heroines in general.

And Lopez can’t celebrate the cult classic’s sexual liberation theme without taking a topless photo of herself, which sees her posing with blind angel Pylar. All in all, JLo looks like she’s having a lot of fun honoring her former co-star’s psychedelic movie.

With how on-point Jennifer Lopez looks as Barbarella, you’d think she was auditioning for the remake of the 1968 film. I mean, she’s wearing each outfit with such pizzazz and poise. However, Sydney Sweeney is set to “save the universe” as the film's lead. The actress seems like a great fit, and I'm confident she'll do a great job embodying the iconic space adventurer.

Per what's known about the remake, Edgar Wright has been in talks to direct, while Kingsman's Jane Goldman and Honey Ross have also been approached to write the screenplay. While the upcoming science-fiction movie is still in its development stages, it’s great that the “On the Floor” singer is already bringing the movie back into the general public's consciousness.

When it comes to the long line of costumes Jennifer Lopez has worn for Halloween over the years, these Barbarella looks may be amongst my favorites. If anything, now I'd like to know how Jane Fonda feels about her former co-star paying tribute to her and her character. In the meantime, anyone who's curious and wants to check out Barbarella can do so by watching the movie for free on Pluto TV.

Just your average South Floridian cinephile who believes the pen is mightier than the sword.
